question:
A 45-year-old female with established erosive rheumatoid arthritis presents with new symptoms over
the past week including daily fevers reaching 38.9°C, pleuritic chest pain, muscle aches, and a new
erythematous facial rash. She denies worsening joint symptoms or morning stiffness. Her current
medications include weekly oral methotrexate 20 mg, weekly subcutaneous etanercept 50 mg (both
providing good control), and daily folic acid. On examination, she has a malar rash and diminished
breath sounds bilaterally at the lung bases. Joint examination reveals no active synovitis. The
remainder of her skin is normal, and there are no oral ulcers. Laboratory testing shows a positive
antinuclear antibody (1:640 titer) and positive anti-double-stranded DNA antibodies. Antihistone
antibody testing is negative. What is the most likely diagnosis? Answer Choices: (A)
Methotrexate-induced pneumonitis (B) Drug-induced lupus (C) Seronegative rheumatoid arthritis with
extra-articular manifestations (D) Etanercept-induced hypersensitivity reaction (E) Idiopathic
pleurocutaneous syndrome (F) Systemic lupus erythematosus (G) Rheumatoid arthritis flare (H) Viral
infection mimicking autoimmune disease (I) Mixed connective tissue disease (J) Rheumatoid arthritis
flare with systemic symptoms
 A. Mixed connective tissue disease
B. Rheumatoid arthritis flare
C. Systemic lupus erythematosus
D. Etanercept-induced hypersensitivity reaction
E. Seronegative rheumatoid arthritis with extra-articular manifestations
F. Rheumatoid arthritis flare with systemic symptoms
G. Idiopathic pleurocutaneous syndrome
H. Methotrexate-induced pneumonitis
I. Viral infection mimicking autoimmune disease
J. Drug-induced lupus
